issues.description: findHue contract is not stated; relative-color syntax exposes the gap
issues.detail: The function's precondition (what node shapes it accepts) and postcondition (which arg position represents 'hue') are implicit. The bug exists because the contract was 'hue is at index 0 or 2' rather than 'hue is at index 0 or 2 of the channel list, where the channel list excludes the from-origin prefix.' State the contract in a comment so future channel-prefix variants do not regress.

issues.description: Channel list and from-prefix are conflated in one args array (leaky abstraction)
issues.detail: args mixes the optional 'from <color>' prefix with the channel triple, forcing every caller to know about offset arithmetic. The right ADT is a ParsedColorFunction with explicit fields {origin, channels}. Extracting that — even as a small helper returning {channels} — removes the index gymnastics and makes future relative-color rules substitutable.

issues.description: isRelativeColor check is structurally weak; a 'from' channel name would false-positive
issues.detail: args[0].value.toLowerCase() === 'from' assumes the first word inside the function can only be the relative-color keyword. CSS syntax guarantees this today, but the invariant is not asserted. A one-line comment citing the CSS Color 5 grammar, or a check that the function is one of HUE_FIRST_ARG_FUNCS/HUE_THIRD_ARG_FUNCS plus arg count >= 4, would document the precondition.

issues.description: Magic offset (2) duplicates knowledge of the from-prefix shape
issues.detail: The literal 2 encodes 'from' + '<origin-color>' = two args. If origin parsing ever yields a different node shape (e.g., a function node already collapses the origin color into one arg, which it does here), the constant is correct only by coincidence. Name it CHANNELS_START_AFTER_FROM or derive it from args.indexOf(args[0]) + 2 with a comment.

issues.description: Test coverage for nested relative colors is thin on the reject side
issues.detail: The accept list includes oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h) and the reject list covers hsl(FROM lch(0 0 10) 0 s l), which is good. Consider one more reject case where the outer function's hue is also wrong and the inner origin is itself a relative color, to lock the recursive postcondition of findHue across nesting.

review.summary: The fix is correct and the tests are well-chosen, but the change exposes that findHue has no written contract. The args array conflates the optional 'from <origin>' prefix with the channel triple, and the patch papers over that with an offset constant. The right ADT is a parsed color function with explicit origin and channels fields; even a small helper would make future relative-color rules substitutable. As a point fix this ships; as architecture it postpones the same bug for the next channel-prefixed syntax.
